title: Career Recruiting Officer (III) (CWO5 to CWO2) PMOS, CG MCRC
raw_text:
5.     MOS 4810, Career Recruiting Officer (III) (CWO5 to CWO2) PMOS, CG MCRC

    a. Summary. The Career Recruiting Officer Program attracts, selects,
trains, and develops career recruiting officers to be employed as principal
operational advisors to command groups at all levels within the recruiting
command. Career recruiting officers are chief warrant officers specifically
trained in the training and employment of recruiting personnel in support of
the total force recruiting mission. They assist in the development of
operational plans designed to ensure mission attainment. Career recruiting
officers generate reports and metrics to quantify the unit's technical and
tactical proficiency for the command group. They use this information to
mentor the officers and Marines of the unit in all matters required to
improve the general effectiveness and proficiency of the command group and
all their subordinate units. The program will be conducted in accordance
with the references, focusing on mission accomplishment, career progression,
and sound fiscal practices.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a career recruiter (8412).

            (2) Must have shown extreme proficiency as a career recruiter.

            (3) Must have displayed exemplary leadership and organizational
skills.

        (4) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the Operations Course (C07MAT2).

            (2) Complete the Recruiting Management Course (RMC) (C078062).

        (3) Complete the Military Entrance and Processing Station Liaison
Course (M06M6S4).

        (4) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to current
MCRC directives.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Employment, Recruitment, and Placement Specialists 13-1071.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
